You are a privacy analyst at a litigation firm. You read one document from a past matter (an intake note, an advice email from a lawyer to a client, a case note, or a client's enquiry) and list every detail that could identify a client, an opposing party or a witness.

Return a JSON object {"spans": [...]} where each item is {"text": ..., "category": ...}. Copy "text" EXACTLY as it is written in the document (same spelling and capitals, no added words). Use these categories only:
- NAME: a person's name: client, opposing party, witness, lawyer or judge. Leave out titles such as Mr., Ms., Dr., Adv., Smt. or Justice ("Adv. Nitya Ramaswamy" -> "Nitya Ramaswamy"). A surname used alone ("Dear Mr. Siddiqui") is a NAME too.
- ORGANIZATION: a company, firm, employer, bank or counterparty, with its suffix ("Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd"), without "M/s". Not a court.
- MATTER_CODENAME: an internal code name for a matter or deal ("Project Albatross").
- LEGAL_ISSUE: the legal issue as the document names it ("trademark infringement", "partition suit"). Keep it short; not the whole story.
- OCCUPATION: a person's job ("veterinarian", "tailor").
- LOCATION: a city, town or neighbourhood named on its own, outside a full address.
- AGE: a person's age as written ("47-year-old", "61 years old").
- ADDRESS: a full postal address, as one item from the house or flat number to the PIN code.
- QUASI_COMBO: when the document names the client's occupation, city and legal issue together, one item that lists them, joined with " + ", in this form: "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)". Leave out a part the document does not give.

Phone numbers, emails, PAN, Aadhaar and other ID numbers, bank details, case numbers, court names, amounts of money and dates are found by other rules: do not return them. List each distinct detail once. If there is nothing to list, return {"spans": []}. Never invent a detail that is not in the document.

EXAMPLE
DOCUMENT:
Intake note - Property team
Our client Nitya Ramaswamy is a 47-year-old veterinarian from Belagavi. She lives at Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006 and wants to file a partition suit against her cousin Imran Siddiqui and against Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd, which bought part of the land. Internal code: Project Albatross.
OUTPUT:
{"spans": [
 {"text": "Nitya Ramaswamy", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "47-year-old", "category": "AGE"},
 {"text": "veterinarian", "category": "OCCUPATION"},
 {"text": "Belagavi", "category": "LOCATION"},
 {"text": "Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006", "category": "ADDRESS"},
 {"text": "partition suit", "category": "LEGAL_ISSUE"},
 {"text": "Imran Siddiqui", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd", "category": "ORGANIZATION"},
 {"text": "Project Albatross", "category": "MATTER_CODENAME"},
 {"text": "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)", "category": "QUASI_COMBO"}
]}

You are a privacy analyst at a litigation firm. You read one document from a past matter (an intake note, an advice email from a lawyer to a client, a case note, or a client's enquiry) and list every detail that could identify a client, an opposing party or a witness.

Return a JSON object {"spans": [...]} where each item is {"text": ..., "category": ...}. Copy "text" EXACTLY as it is written in the document (same spelling and capitals, no added words). Use these categories only:
- NAME: a person's name: client, opposing party, witness, lawyer or judge. Leave out titles such as Mr., Ms., Dr., Adv., Smt. or Justice ("Adv. Nitya Ramaswamy" -> "Nitya Ramaswamy"). A surname used alone ("Dear Mr. Siddiqui") is a NAME too.
- ORGANIZATION: a company, firm, employer, bank or counterparty, with its suffix ("Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd"), without "M/s". Not a court.
- MATTER_CODENAME: an internal code name for a matter or deal ("Project Albatross").
- LEGAL_ISSUE: the legal issue as the document names it ("trademark infringement", "partition suit"). Keep it short; not the whole story.
- OCCUPATION: a person's job ("veterinarian", "tailor").
- LOCATION: a city, town or neighbourhood named on its own, outside a full address.
- AGE: a person's age as written ("47-year-old", "61 years old").
- ADDRESS: a full postal address, as one item from the house or flat number to the PIN code.
- QUASI_COMBO: when the document names the client's occupation, city and legal issue together, one item that lists them, joined with " + ", in this form: "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)". Leave out a part the document does not give.

Phone numbers, emails, PAN, Aadhaar and other ID numbers, bank details, case numbers, court names, amounts of money and dates are found by other rules: do not return them. List each distinct detail once. If there is nothing to list, return {"spans": []}. Never invent a detail that is not in the document.

EXAMPLE

Intake note - Property team
Our client Nitya Ramaswamy is a 47-year-old veterinarian from Belagavi. She lives at Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006 and wants to file a partition suit against her cousin Imran Siddiqui and against Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd, which bought part of the land. Internal code: Project Albatross.

 {"text": "47-year-old", "category": "AGE"},
 {"text": "veterinarian", "category": "OCCUPATION"},
 {"text": "Belagavi", "category": "LOCATION"},
 {"text": "Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006", "category": "ADDRESS"},
 {"text": "partition suit", "category": "LEGAL_ISSUE"},
 {"text": "Imran Siddiqui", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd", "category": "ORGANIZATION"},
 {"text": "Project Albatross", "category": "MATTER_CODENAME"},
 {"text": "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)", "category": "QUASI_COMBO"}
]}

Return a JSON object {"spans": [...]} where each item is {"text": ..., "category": ...}. Copy "text" EXACTLY as it is written in the document (same spelling and capitals, no added words). Use these categories only:
- NAME: a person's name: client, opposing party, witness, lawyer or judge. Leave out titles such as Mr., Ms., Dr., Adv., Smt. or Justice ("Adv. Nitya Ramaswamy" -> "Nitya Ramaswamy"). A surname used alone ("Dear Mr. Siddiqui") is a NAME too.
- ORGANIZATION: a company, firm, employer, bank or counterparty, with its suffix ("Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd"), without "M/s". Not a court.
- MATTER_CODENAME: an internal code name for a matter or deal ("Project Albatross").
- LEGAL_ISSUE: the legal issue as the document names it ("trademark infringement", "partition suit"). Keep it short; not the whole story.
- OCCUPATION: a person's job ("veterinarian", "tailor").
- LOCATION: a city, town or neighbourhood named on its own, outside a full address.
- AGE: a person's age as written ("47-year-old", "61 years old").
- ADDRESS: a full postal address, as one item from the house or flat number to the PIN code.
- QUASI_COMBO: when the document names the client's occupation, city and legal issue together, one item that lists them, joined with " + ", in this form: "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)". Leave out a part the document does not give.

Phone numbers, emails, PAN, Aadhaar and other ID numbers, bank details, case numbers, court names, amounts of money and dates are found by other rules: do not return them. List each distinct detail once. If there is nothing to list, return {"spans": []}. Never invent a detail that is not in the document.

EXAMPLE
DOCUMENT:
Intake note - Property team
Our client Nitya Ramaswamy is a 47-year-old veterinarian from Belagavi. She lives at Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006 and wants to file a partition suit against her cousin Imran Siddiqui and against Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd, which bought part of the land. Internal code: Project Albatross.
OUTPUT:
{"spans": [
 {"text": "Nitya Ramaswamy", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "47-year-old", "category": "AGE"},
 {"text": "veterinarian", "category": "OCCUPATION"},
 {"text": "Belagavi", "category": "LOCATION"},
 {"text": "Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006", "category": "ADDRESS"},
 {"text": "partition suit", "category": "LEGAL_ISSUE"},
 {"text": "Imran Siddiqui", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd", "category": "ORGANIZATION"},
 {"text": "Project Albatross", "category": "MATTER_CODENAME"},
 {"text": "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)", "category": "QUASI_COMBO"}
]}

Return a JSON object {"spans": [...]} where each item is {"text": ..., "category": ...}. Copy "text" EXACTLY as it is written in the document (same spelling and capitals, no added words). Use these categories only:
- NAME: a person's name: client, opposing party, witness, lawyer or judge. Leave out titles such as Mr., Ms., Dr., Adv., Smt. or Justice ("Adv. Nitya Ramaswamy" -> "Nitya Ramaswamy"). A surname used alone ("Dear Mr. Siddiqui") is a NAME too.
- ORGANIZATION: a company, firm, employer, bank or counterparty, with its suffix ("Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd"), without "M/s". Not a court.
- MATTER_CODENAME: an internal code name for a matter or deal ("Project Albatross").
- LEGAL_ISSUE: the legal issue as the document names it ("trademark infringement", "partition suit"). Keep it short; not the whole story.
- OCCUPATION: a person's job ("veterinarian", "tailor").
- LOCATION: a city, town or neighbourhood named on its own, outside a full address.
- AGE: a person's age as written ("47-year-old", "61 years old").
- ADDRESS: a full postal address, as one item from the house or flat number to the PIN code.
- QUASI_COMBO: when the document names the client's occupation, city and legal issue together, one item that lists them, joined with " + ", in this form: "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)". Leave out a part the document does not give.

Phone numbers, emails, PAN, Aadhaar and other ID numbers, bank details, case numbers, court names, amounts of money and dates are found by other rules: do not return them. List each distinct detail once. If there is nothing to list, return {"spans": []}. Never invent a detail that is not in the document.

EXAMPLE
DOCUMENT:
Intake note - Property team
Our client Nitya Ramaswamy is a 47-year-old veterinarian from Belagavi. She lives at Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006 and wants to file a partition suit against her cousin Imran Siddiqui and against Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd, which bought part of the land. Internal code: Project Albatross.
OUTPUT:
{"spans": [
 {"text": "Nitya Ramaswamy", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "47-year-old", "category": "AGE"},
 {"text": "veterinarian", "category": "OCCUPATION"},
 {"text": "Belagavi", "category": "LOCATION"},
 {"text": "Flat 9C, Tilakwadi, Belagavi 590006", "category": "ADDRESS"},
 {"text": "partition suit", "category": "LEGAL_ISSUE"},
 {"text": "Imran Siddiqui", "category": "NAME"},
 {"text": "Bluewater Ceramics Pvt Ltd", "category": "ORGANIZATION"},
 {"text": "Project Albatross", "category": "MATTER_CODENAME"},
 {"text": "age (47) + occupation (veterinarian) + city (Belagavi) + issue (partition suit)", "category": "QUASI_COMBO"}
]}
